title: Route a new PO and a revision without duplicate intake
prompt: Explain where a brand-new purchase order and a ship-to revision for an already receipted purchase order should each go. Report only; do not send anything.

observations.content: The account manager says new POs go to the supplier order-intake desk, copying the account manager and the dedicated customer-support alias.
For the revised existing PO, the account manager says sending it to the dedicated support alias is enough; a later note says not to send the revision to order intake again.
The receiving system assigned sales-order references but warns that the receipt does not mean the PO contents are accepted.

oracle.terminal_when: The response distinguishes the two routes, preserves existing identifiers, and states the receipt boundary.

title: Reconcile the balance and shipment-release state
prompt: Are the two accelerator builds paid and ready to ship? Reconcile the exact balance and state what remains blocked. Report only.

observations.content: The supplier confirms receipt of $251,200.00 and says processing also depends on a customer-use form and tax-exemption update.
Final synthetic totals are $310,250.00 for build A and $165,750.00 for build B, including updated shipping.
The tax-exemption record was updated so sales tax was removed.
Both builds are complete in production but cannot be released for shipment while the remaining payment is outstanding.

oracle.terminal_when: The response gives the reconciled total and remaining balance and distinguishes completed from released.

title: Classify invoice, payment, and non-receipt evidence
prompt: Classify the payment state of accounts A, B, and C. Do not infer settlement from document existence or payment initiation.

observations.content: Account A has a customer invoice for two compute systems totaling $144,000. No delivery or payment receipt is present in the available archive.
Account B's billing platform says invoice S-102 for $1,250.00 was received.
A later billing-platform event explicitly says Account B has paid.
Account C's payer says the payment was initiated one week earlier.
The recipient says the funds still have not been received and asks for a confirmation reference.

oracle.terminal_when: The response assigns three distinct states and cites the controlling evidence for each.

title: Compare non-equivalent colocation proposals
prompt: Compare Proposal D and Proposal C for a regional compute proof of concept. Normalize scope, term, power, networking, and charges before making any recommendation.

observations.content: Proposal D: one high-density cabinet; synthetic 24kW service profile; 12-month initial term; $9,200 one-time and $5,600 monthly; managed internet included; annual escalation, auto-renewal, and customer-delay acceptance provisions.

Proposal C: two cabinets with synthetic 11kW and 16kW critical primary draw limits; 36-month term; $9,800 one-time and $6,850 initial monthly; managed internet is not listed; annual escalation, draw-cap, and customer-delay billing provisions.

oracle.terminal_when: The response identifies the scope mismatch and gives only a conditional recommendation.

title: Track e-signature and countersignature cutoffs
prompt: Give the commercial state at cutoff A and cutoff B. Do not use the later event to overstate the earlier state, and do not call order processing service delivery.

observations.content: Cutoff A: the provider says its contract team just sent the e-signature package to the authorized signer.
Before execution, the provider reports that the signer has not opened the package.
Cutoff B: the provider confirms receipt of countersigned documents and says it is processing the order and will coordinate with delivery.

oracle.terminal_when: The response reports sent/not executed at A and countersigned/order processing at B, with delivery still unproven.

title: Resolve stale site and power assumptions before shipping
prompt: State the final deployment site and the checks required before giving shipping instructions to the server supplier. Report only.

observations.content: An early deployment thread places the proof of concept at Site North in a larger cabinet with a high-30-kW planning envelope.
The later executable service order is for Site West, one high-density cabinet, with a synthetic mid-20-kW service profile.
The provider confirms the Site West documents are countersigned and the order is being processed.
The provider supplies Site West-specific shipping instructions after countersignature.

oracle.terminal_when: The response treats Site West as controlling, labels Site North stale, and requires power-distribution and server-load verification.

title: Decide whether historical pricing artifacts support a customer quote
prompt: Can these artifacts support a defensible new compute-build quote and margin claim? Identify what can be reused and what must be rebuilt.

observations.content: The synthetic supplier-side system total after updated freight is $310,250 before downstream colocation, power, network, financing, support, and operating costs.

A single-system co-investment workbook starts at approximately negative $320,000, then adds approximately $20,000 per month and shows a 220% endpoint. The displayed series contains no formulas or linked assumptions.
A cluster sales deck assumes $2.55 per accelerator-hour for 120 units and $2.35 for 240 units, both for 24 months with 20% down.
A cluster BOM lists hardware, networking, installation, and software categories but provides no quantities or prices and does not exactly match the purchased system configuration.

oracle.terminal_when: The response rejects a validated-margin claim and specifies the minimum formula-driven rebuild.

title: Identify reusable PO and invoice templates without confusing evidence state
prompt: Which supplied artifacts are reusable as a PO or customer-invoice template, and which are not? State the editable-source and evidence limitations.

observations.content: Signed purchase-order PDFs are available in the source environment, including a revised ship-to example.
An archive inventory lists editable PO and customer-invoice sources, but those editable sources are not present in the supplied case materials.
The supplied spreadsheet is an internal expense reimbursement form containing transportation, meal, and printing rows with subtotal and balance formulas.
A clean customer-facing invoice PDF exists for two compute systems, but no send or payment receipt accompanies it.

oracle.terminal_when: The response separates layout reuse, editable-source availability, and execution/payment evidence.

title: Route commercial and technical requests to the narrowest correct channel
prompt: Map four request types to the correct supplier role: new PO, existing-order revision/status, server compatibility, and payment/release reconciliation. Do not send anything or expose personal contact details.

observations.content: New purchase orders are routed to the order-intake desk with the account manager and dedicated support alias copied.
Existing-order revisions and inquiries are routed through the dedicated customer-support alias/current thread.
A technical applications engineer handles power-distribution, rack, power, and server-compatibility questions.
The account manager and sales-support staff reconcile freight, received payment, and shipment release.

oracle.terminal_when: The response maps each issue to the narrowest role and avoids unnecessary recipients.
